# agentmail_api_key (Ephemeral Resource)

Mints an AgentMail API key without writing its secret to plan or state.

Terraform opens ephemeral resources during `plan` as well as `apply`, so **every plan and every apply mints a new key**, and the provider's own key needs the `api_key_create` permission at plan time. By default the key is revoked when Terraform closes the resource at the end of the run, which suits handing it to another provider configuration. To store the key somewhere that outlives the run, set `revoke_on_close = false` with `ttl` or `expires_at`, and gate the resource with `count` so it mints only when you rotate.

A key can't outlive the key that mints it. Without `ttl` or `expires_at` it inherits the provider key's expiry, and never expires when that key never does.

## Example Usage

```terraform
# A short-lived key that can only manage inboxes, handed to a second provider
# configuration. It is revoked when the run ends.
ephemeral "agentmail_api_key" "inboxes" {
  name        = "terraform-inboxes"
  permissions = ["inbox_read", "inbox_create", "inbox_update", "inbox_delete"]
  ttl         = "1h"
}

provider "agentmail" {
  alias   = "inboxes"
  api_key = ephemeral.agentmail_api_key.inboxes.api_key
}

resource "agentmail_inbox" "support" {
  provider = agentmail.inboxes
  username = "support"
}

# A key for CI that outlives the run, stored through a write-only attribute
# so it never reaches state. Every plan and apply would mint a new key, so it
# is minted only when rotate_ci_key is true, and it expires on its own. A
# rotation's plan mints a key too, which stays valid until it expires; keep
# ttl short enough for that.
variable "rotate_ci_key" {
  type    = bool
  default = false
}

variable "ci_key_version" {
  type = number
}

ephemeral "agentmail_api_key" "ci" {
  count = var.rotate_ci_key ? 1 : 0

  name            = "ci"
  permissions     = ["inbox_read", "message_send"]
  ttl             = "2160h"
  revoke_on_close = false
}

resource "aws_secretsmanager_secret_version" "ci_agentmail_key" {
  secret_id                = "ci/agentmail-api-key"
  secret_string_wo         = var.rotate_ci_key ? ephemeral.agentmail_api_key.ci[0].api_key : null
  secret_string_wo_version = var.ci_key_version
}
```

<!-- schema generated by tfplugindocs -->
## Schema

### Optional

- `expires_at` (String) When the key expires, in RFC 3339. Set it or `ttl`, or read the inherited expiry here. AgentMail can't change it afterwards.
- `inbox_id` (String) Scope the key to this inbox.
- `name` (String) The key's name.
- `permissions` (Set of String) The permissions to grant, such as `inbox_read` or `message_send`. **Unset grants every permission**, intersected with the key's scope. A key can't grant permissions its creator lacks.
- `pod_id` (String) Scope the key to this pod. Leave both `pod_id` and `inbox_id` unset for an organization key.
- `revoke_on_close` (Boolean) Revoke the key when Terraform closes the resource at the end of the run. Defaults to `true`. Setting `false` requires `ttl` or `expires_at`.
- `ttl` (String) How long the key lives, as a Go duration such as `720h`.

### Read-Only

- `api_key` (String, Sensitive) The secret. AgentMail returns it only when the key is created.
- `api_key_id` (String) The key's ID.
- `created_at` (String) When the key was created, in RFC 3339.
- `prefix` (String) The secret's prefix, which AgentMail shows to identify the key.
